manifest.title: Lathe
manifest.author: Adam Smith
manifest.description: Coding agent tools (lathe, bash, read, write, edit, glob, grep, view, peek, poke, interpret, onboard, expose, destroy) backed by per-user sandbox VMs with transparent lifecycle management.

specs.name: bash
specs.description:
Execute a bash command in the sandbox. Non-interactive only.
Each call uses a fresh non-login Bash shell; rc files are not sourced and
shell state (such as exports and cd) does not persist between calls.
Runs with set -e -o pipefail: an unhandled command or pipeline failure can
abort the remaining script. Handle expected probe failures explicitly
(for example, with if); use && for commands with dependent prerequisites.
Nonzero command exits return an exit status and captured output, distinct
from errors launching or observing execution.
Commands that finish within the foreground window return output directly.
Long-running commands auto-background and return a descriptor with log
file paths for monitoring. Text previews are capped at 50 KiB. Full logs and
exit status remain readable for 24 hours after completion, until a later
bash call reaps expired evidence. Sandbox stop/restart clears these files.

For first-time application setup, read lathe(manpage="services") before
installing or launching; it routes to relevant skills and the configured
handbook. Inspection commands may come first.

foreground_seconds.description: Seconds to wait before auto-backgrounding. Omit or set -1 to use the server default. Set 0 for immediate background (fire-and-forget). Use higher positive values for known-slow commands.

specs.name: destroy
specs.description:
Permanently destroy the sandbox VM. Irreversible.
Prompts the user for confirmation before proceeding.

specs.name: edit
specs.description: Edit a file by exact string replacement. Fails on ambiguous matches unless replace_all=true.

specs.name: expose
specs.description:
Expose an already-running HTTP/WebSocket service. Does not install or start applications.
For user file upload/download, interactive shells, browser VS Code IDEs,
or static websites, first read lathe(manpage="services") for lifecycle
guidance and optional handbook references, then launch with bash.

target.description: "http:<port>" for an already-running HTTP service on port 1024–65535, or "vnc" for Daytona's built-in desktop (start with poke first). See the services/computer manuals for lifecycle and access safeguards.

access.description: Required policy: "private" authenticates the owner and fails closed; "public" allows anyone with the URL and may fall back to a direct bearer URL. Choose private unless the user explicitly approves public/world access. Shells, IDEs and VNC desktops should stay private: a public desktop grants control of logged-in accounts.

tag.description: Optional untrusted hostname hint: lowercase letters, digits, internal hyphens, max 32 characters. Hostname text never proves identity or purpose.

upstream_headers.description: Fixed values injected into every HTTP request/WebSocket handshake, for credentials the browser cannot hold (e.g. Authorization for an app with no login). Not needed for forwarding: browser headers the app's own pages send already pass through; never inject a CSRF marker. Replaces browser values case-insensitively. Requires a compatible wrapper, never direct fallback. Max 16 headers, 64-byte names, printable ASCII values up to 4096 bytes, 8192 bytes total. Routing/transport headers forbidden. Values remain in tool arguments; see services manual for trust boundaries.

public_headers_acknowledged.description: Required true when access is "public" and upstream_headers is nonempty: every visitor then acts with the injected values. Set only after the user approves that.

specs.name: glob
specs.description:
Search for files in the sandbox workspace by glob pattern.
Thin ripgrep --files adapter: returns bounded absolute paths, not exhaustive
counts. Uses rg ignore/hidden-file rules and traversal order.

pattern.description: One workspace-relative ripgrep glob, e.g. '**/*.py' or '*.{js,ts}'. No comma-separated pattern language. rg supports braces and ! exclusion. Use bash with rg for multiple globs, hidden/ignored files, or other roots.

max_lines.description: Max concrete result lines, excluding the summary header (default: 100, clamped to 1–500).

specs.name: grep
specs.description:
Search file contents in the sandbox workspace by regex.
Thin ripgrep adapter: returns bounded absolute path:line:text hits with
rg regex, ignore and binary-file semantics. Stops at the result limit,
without exhaustive counts. Long matches use rg's 200-column preview.

pattern.description: Ripgrep regex, e.g. 'import.*asyncio' or 'TODO|FIXME'. No Python lookaround/backreferences.

files.description: One workspace-relative ripgrep glob (default: '**/*'); braces supported. Use bash with rg for multiple globs, hidden/ignored files, or other roots.

max_lines.description: Max concrete result lines, excluding the summary header (default: 100, clamped to 1–500).

specs.name: interpret
specs.description:
Run Python code in a persistent REPL session. Variables, imports, and
definitions survive across calls within the same conversation, across OWUI
workers and toolkit reloads. Use this for iterative data exploration and
incremental computation. For one-shot scripts, prefer bash().
One execution per conversation at a time; overlapping calls return busy.
Execution and its bounded result survive an OWUI worker exiting. Completed
run records remain in the sandbox for 24 hours, until a later submission.
Output is a 50 KiB preview; excess output is discarded explicitly.
Write large results to a sandbox file for read() or expose().

code.description: Python code to execute. Top-level await is not supported.

timeout.description: Max execution time in seconds (default: 120). Use 0 for no limit. A timeout discards Python memory; partial effects may remain.

specs.name: lathe
specs.description: Read operational orientation or a task-specific manual page.

manpage.description: "overview" for safeguards and page index; "interpret", "background", "services", "computer", "egress" for details; "version" for installed version.

specs.name: onboard
specs.description:
Load project listing, AGENTS.md, and shared, Lathe-specific, and project skills.
Read relevant SKILL.md files for full instructions. Skip repeat onboarding
when the supplied context already covers this project.

specs.name: peek
specs.description:
Observe the shared Chromium browser (the user can watch it) and the sandbox desktop. Never starts or changes anything.
Browser first: page.text reads a tab's visible text, page.wait waits for text, a selector or a URL, page.list lists tabs.
Screenshots return images; other commands return text. Read lathe(manpage="computer") before first use.

command.description: Browser, with args: page.list {}; page.wait {text?: str, selector?: str, url?: str, gone?: str, timeout?: int 1-30 = 10, tab?: str}, exactly one of text/selector/url/gone; page.text {tab?: str, selector?: str, maxChars?: int 100-200000 = 20000}. Desktop (args in lathe(manpage="computer")): status, screenshot, screenshot.compressed, accessibility.tree, accessibility.find, display.info, mouse.position. Diagnostics: display.windows, process.status/logs/errors.

args.description: Command-specific JSON object. Strict types; unknown fields are rejected. Coordinates are native desktop pixels.

specs.name: poke
specs.description:
Act in a real, shared Chromium browser (the user can watch it) or on the sandbox desktop.
Use the browser when curl is not enough: JavaScript-rendered sites, bot challenges or 403s, logins, downloads needing browser cookies.
page.open launches it (starting the desktop if down); then page.click, page.type, page.save (url: fetch bytes with browser cookies; no url: save the tab as pdf/html/mhtml), page.eval (awaits promises).
Read lathe(manpage="computer") before first use. Pause all input and screenshots during human login; resume only after the user says ready.
Ask before first browser use unless requested, and before desktop input beyond it; once allowed, offer expose(target="vnc", access="private") as a live view.

command.description: Browser, with args: page.open {url: URL, tab?: str, newTab?: bool}; page.click {text?: str, selector?: str, tab?: str}, exactly one of text/selector; page.type {selector: str, text: str, submit?: bool, tab?: str}; page.save {path: absolute path, format?: pdf|html|mhtml, url?: URL, tab?: str}, at most one of url/format; page.eval {js: str, tab?: str}. Desktop (args in lathe(manpage="computer")): mouse.click/move/drag/scroll/down/up, keyboard.type/press/hotkey/down/up, accessibility.focus/invoke/set_value. Lifecycle: start, stop, process.restart.

args.description: Command-specific JSON object. Strict types; unknown fields are rejected. Never put passwords in tool arguments.

specs.name: read
specs.description:
Read a file from the sandbox. Returns numbered lines, capped at 2000 lines
and 50 KiB of text. A clipped preview is explicitly labeled; the original
file remains available via bash byte ranges or expose().
Supports Python-style negative indexing: start=-10 reads from
10 lines before the end, stop=-3 stops 3 lines before the end.
All positive values are 1-indexed. stop is exclusive (half-open).
stop=0 (default) means end of file.

start.description: First line to return (1-indexed). Negative counts from end. 0 is treated as 1.

stop.description: Line to stop before (exclusive, 1-indexed). Negative counts from end. 0 means end of file.

specs.name: view
specs.description:
View an image file from the sandbox, loading it into your visual context.
Use for screenshots, charts, rendered pages, or generated images.
Requires a vision-capable model; if the current model cannot accept image
input, the call is refused with a reminder instead of the image.
Supported formats: PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP (detected from file contents, not
extension). Max 4 MB; downscale larger images first via bash (e.g. with
ImageMagick or Pillow).

path.description: Absolute path to the image file.

specs.name: write
specs.description:
Write a file to the sandbox (creates parents automatically).

For large files, prefer a skeleton-then-edit workflow: write the file first
with overall structure and ``# PLACEHOLDER: <section>`` markers, then use
``edit()`` to expand each placeholder incrementally. This makes progress
visible to the user in real time and keeps partial work on disk if
generation is interrupted.
